title: Honest question: do you guys actually buy games that you know use AI?
author: johnkernelle
selftext:
As devs using AI, it’s easy to love these tools because of how much time they save and how much easier they make gamedev.



But putting your dev hat aside and looking at things strictly as a gamer/consumer,

do you actually buy games when you clearly know its vibecoded, and AI was used in them?



Cause looking at other gaming subs during events like Steam Next Festt,

where it feels like a huge chunk of the new games are AI-made,

a lot of gamers still really hate AI in games.

comments.author: 0DayMaker
comments.body: I'm gonna take a wild guess that anyone buying AAA games has, at least unknowingly, paid for games made with a lot of AI assistance. Knowingly? No I haven't personally.

replies.author: Grand_Sprinkles_2094
replies.body: Xbox employee told they use AI for games 😂😂 but gaming industry is the only one who keeps it quiet

comments.author: NicoparaDEV
comments.body: I know for a fact that adult game players will eat anything with a pussy

replies.author: LostRequirement4828
replies.body: Might be the best way to make money, not gonna lie, lol

comments.author: zomgmeister
comments.body: Not buying a lot of any games nowadays, got a huge backlog and lack of time, but usage of AI is definitely not a factor for me in such a decision.

comments.author: Vegetable_Voice_2044
comments.body: If you won't play a game that uses ai, you can just give up the hobby entirely. It's the way of the future wether folks like it or not.

comments.author: magic6435
comments.body: Not sure there is such a thing as AAA game without AI published in the last 12 months

comments.author: Navadvisor
comments.body: The thing is, if you think it's vibe coded it's probably a shitty game. Not to mention it still takes months to years to make a good game even with AI, so its not even been a year yet since we've had good AI and the models from October are miles above the models from February. I absolutely would play a game made with AI, but just like some garbage asset flip I don't want some garbage AI game.

replies.author: ichivictus
replies.body: Agreed. My game took 3 to 4 months of basically full time work with a lot of ai to get to a place that I am happy to share. Another 2 months to be prepared to sell. And it still feels like an indie game but polished. 2 months in it felt like a prototype.

comments.author: Artanox
comments.body: There is no reason not to, but the market will soon or later shift to free products.

comments.author: Grand_Sprinkles_2094
comments.body: Yes, I’d buy it if it’s fun don’t care if human or ai wrote the code

comments.author: fued
comments.body: I dont care if AI has been used or not, but AI being used and being obvious is a very obvious sign that it is low effort garbage.

comments.author: MrTheWaffleKing
comments.body: I’ve seen two here that I’m excited for release. I’m in game dev to share my game dev experience to make the perfect games for myself, to learn the nuances others are working thru, more than to find new games

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body: To me there is a bigger issue, i havn’t bought a game since i started using ai to make stuff. I was already way off the aaa 60 dollar game wagon and only buying indie and early access stuff and now i can get essentially same quality as early access in my spare time over a few weeks and it’s got the design choices that i want so i don’t have to go “oh man, so close. If they had just done x.”

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body:
reddit is a very small percentage of gamers, and reddit indie gaming subs are very developer focused, which are even more anti-ai, as understandably their own livelihoods are at stake. 

We're definitely moving toward a general consumer base that does not care if AI is used, AS LONG AS the game itself looks/is fun and not blatantly AI SLOP.  

And for people working with AI a lot... just remember, what looks slightly AI sloppy to you, looks very blatantly AI sloppy to others.

comments.author: jivenossauro
comments.body: I bought crimson desert. If they did not use AI on that, they used slaves and possibly some trained animals

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Yes. I either own or have spent money on:

Call of Duty, Stellaris, Where Winds Meet, Crimson Desert, Dark and Darker, Throne and Liberty, EVE (admittedly a long time ago), X4, Sins of a Solar Empire, Anno, Dragonsword, Story of Seasons, Esports Godfather, etc. 

And those are just the handful or so most popular that have actually disclosed their AI use. You can expect that many game companies are utilizing it but have high enough quality control that no one can actually call them out on it. 

XBox's senior business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup had several X posts recently on this basically calling out  the industry and saying they were all using it and pushing for them to just admit it so we could move on. His profile has since been taken down, but the records are available. But the games he's worked on have not disclosed their AI use, which just reiterates that it's an open secret.

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body: I don't spend money on games where a majority of the creative work is offloaded to AI. Why would you? Heavy vibecoding isn't quite so ick, but I'd still be suspicious in regard to quality and security.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
I will do you one better:

If these games, posted here which I played this month, become polished products:

\- Abyss  
\- Chromedrift  
\- Bloodline Shadows

I will instantly buy them. They are on extremely solid foundations and almost certainly will some of the best value for money I've spent on video games.

I do not give one single fck about the method of production. I care about the craft and the execution.

EDIT: I mean I guess I should qualify that a bit. Like, if it turns out your game was made by enslaved children or something, well obviously then I'm not buying it. If you donate the proceeds to the Mossad, I'm not buying it. 

But as far as the medium of creation goes? Whatever. You could have wished the game from a Djinn for all I care so long as it's clear you meant it, and the game shows the level of love and care and desire to create something special that can only come from art made with passion no matter what tools were deployed.
